answer: Sequential workload escrow: each identity must complete a randomized micro-task queue before its outputs are accepted, with results chained to a public relic of prior completion. Clones inherit the queue position of their parent, so splitting multiplies waiting time and compute. Tasks verify against a shared trellis of dependency hashes, making forged histories detectable. An attacker cloning N identities pays N times the queue compute plus abandonment penalties, while each clone still lands on the same reef of saturated task slots.
